                "headline": "Coastal Flood Warning issued September 26 at 11:51AM EDT until September 27 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ",
                "description": "* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to two feet of\ninundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines\nand tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking\nwaves of up to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip\nCurrent Risk, dangerous rip currents.\n\n* WHERE...Delaware Beaches.\n\n* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 PM EDT Sunday.\nFor the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Sunday. For the\nHigh Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in\ncoastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal\nwaterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to\nvulnerable structures may begin to occur. Dangerous swimming\nand surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip\ncurrents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into\ndeeper water.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant beach erosion is expected.\nBreaching of sand dunes is possible.",
                "instruction": "A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal\nflooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water\nlevels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.\nFollow the recommendations of local emergency management\nofficials.\n\nDo not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be\ndeeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in\ndanger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly\nrepairs.\n\nVisit the National Water Prediction Service at\nhttps://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and\nflood impact information for your local tide gauge.\n\nInexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to\ndangerous surf conditions.\n\nAlways obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,\nalways have a floatation device with you and swim near a\nlifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and\nfloat and do not swim against the current.                 "description": "* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to two feet of\ninundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines\nand tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking\nwaves of up to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip\nCurrent Risk, dangerous rip currents.\n\n* WHERE...Atlantic Coastal Cape May and Coastal Atlantic.\n\n* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 PM EDT Sunday.\nFor the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Sunday. For the\nHigh Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in\ncoastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal\nwaterways. Rip\ncurrents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into\ndeeper water.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant beach erosion is expected.\nBreaching of sand dunes is possible.",
                "instruction": "A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal\nflooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water\nlevels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.\nFollow the recommendations of local emergency management\nofficials.\n\nDo not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be\ndeeper than you think it is. If you enter the surf zone,\nalways have a floatation device with you and swim near a\nlifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and\nfloat and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel\nto the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or\nwave for help.",

                "description": "* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to two feet of\ninundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines\nand tidal waterways.                 "senderName": "NWS Honolulu HI",
                "headline": "Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 26 at 5:16AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI",
                "description": "HLSHFO\n\nThis product covers the Hawaiian islands\n\n**NOLO REMAINS NEARLY STATIONARY SOUTH OF THE BIG ISLAND**\n\n\nNEW INFORMATION\n---------------\n\n* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:\n- None\n\n* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:\n- A Tropical Storm Warning and Hurricane Watch are in effect for\nBig Island East, Big Island Interior, Big Island North, Big\nIsland South, Big Island Southeast, Big Island Summits, Kohala,\nand Kona\n- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Haleakala Summit,\nKahoolawe, Kipahulu, Lanai Leeward, Lanai Mauka, Lanai South,\nLanai Windward, Maui Central Valley North, Maui Central Valley\nSouth, Maui Leeward West, Maui Windward West, Molokai Leeward\nSouth, Molokai North, Molokai Southeast, Molokai West, Molokai\nWindward, South Haleakala, South Maui/Upcountry, and Windward\nHaleakala\n\n* STORM INFORMATION:\n- About 340 miles south-southeast of Honolulu or about 200 miles\nsouth of Hilo\n- 16.9N 155.5W\n- Storm Intensity 105 mph\n- Movement Stationary\n\nSITUATION OVERVIEW\n------------------\n\nNearly stationary, Hurricane Nolo is expected to strengthen into a\nmajor hurricane as it turns westward and accelerates later today and\nSunday. Nolo is forecast to track northward early next week and weaken.\nWhile the center will stay well south and west of the state, impacts\nwill extend far outside the center of Nolo.\n\nBands of intense showers and thunderstorms will bring an additional\n6 to 8 inches of rainfall with localized higher amounts of 10 inches\nto windward and southeast portions of the Big Island. This heavy\nrainfall will cause significant, life-threatening flash flooding and\nmudslides, particularly in areas of steep terrain. Isolated heavy rain\nwill spread to Maui, bringing an additional 1 to 2 inches of rainfall\nwith locally higher amounts of 4 inches possible, especially over\nsteep terrain. Terrain-enhanced rainfall from outer rain bands may\nalso reach the rest of the state.\n\nTropical storm force winds and gusts continue across the Big Island,\nand may reach hurricane strength today, especially over complex\nterrain. A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Maui County, where\ntropical storm force winds and gusts are occurring due to terrain\nenhancements. Strong, gusty winds will affect all Hawaiian Islands\nthrough the weekend, and a Wind Advisory is now in effect for the\nremaining Hawaiian Islands.\n\nSwells generated by Nolo will bring dangerously large, rough surf and\nsevere rip currents, especially for southeast and east facing shores\nof Big Island and Maui. A High Surf Advisory remains in effect for\nsoutheast and east facing shores of Big Island and Maui as well as\neast facing shores of Molokai, Kauai and Oahu.\n\nTornadoes and waterspouts are possible near and over the Big Island,\nprimarily to the right of the track of Nolo.\n\nPOTENTIAL IMPACTS\n-----------------\n\n* FLOODING RAIN:\nPotential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across\nwindward and southeast Big Island. Remain well guarded against\ndangerous flood waters having possible significant impacts. If\nrealized, these impacts include:\n- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and\nrescues.\n- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter\ncurrents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially\nin usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals,\narroyos, and ditches overflow.\n- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.\nSeveral places may experience expanded areas of rapid\ninundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage\nareas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as\nstorm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions\nbecome hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.\n\nPotential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across\nwindward and southeast Big Island and portions of Maui. Remain well\nguarded against locally hazardous flood waters having possible limited\nimpacts.\n\n* WIND:\nPotential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across Big\nIsland and Maui. Remain well sheltered from dangerous wind having\npossible significant impacts. If realized, these impacts include:\n- Some damage to roofing and siding materials, along with damage\nto porches, awnings, carports, and sheds. A few buildings\nexperiencing window, door, and garage door failures. Mobile\nhomes damaged, especially if unanchored. Unsecured lightweight\nobjects become dangerous projectiles.\n- Several large trees snapped or uprooted, but with greater\nnumbers in places where trees are shallow rooted. Several\nfences and roadway signs blown over.\n- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban\nor heavily wooded places. A few bridges, causeways, and access\nroutes impassable.\n- Scattered power and communications outages, but more prevalent\nin areas with above ground lines.\n\nPotential indirect impacts from the main wind event are also now\nunfolding across the rest of the state. Remain well sheltered from\nhazardous wind having possible limited impacts.\n\n\n* SURGE:\nPotential impacts from the main surge event are now unfolding across\nsoutheast Big Island. Remain well away from locally hazardous surge\nhaving possible limited impacts. If realized, these impacts include:\n- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along\nimmediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas\nfarther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.\n- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread\nwith surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where\nsurge water covers the road.\n- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly\nin usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.\n- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,\nand piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.\n\nElsewhere across the Hawaiian islands, little to no impact is\nanticipated.\n\n* TORNADOES:\nPotential impacts from tornadoes are still unfolding across Big Island.\nRemain well braced against a tornado event having possible limited\nimpacts. If realized, these impacts include:\n- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution\nof emergency plans during tropical events.\n- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power\nand communications disruptions.\n- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys\ntoppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,\nlarge tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees\nknocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats\npulled from moorings.\n\nPRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS\n----------------------------------\n\n* EVACUATIONS:\nFollow the advice of local officials\n\n* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:\nNow is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for\nupdates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a battery-\npowered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.\n\nDuring the peak of the storm be ready to move quickly. Keep your\nshoes on and rain gear handy. Boots and athletic shoes offer the best\nfoot protection if you become unexpectedly exposed to the weather.\n\nKeep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose\npower, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and\ncheck-ins.\n\nDo not venture outside while in the eye of a hurricane as any\nimprovement in weather will only be temporary. Once the eye passes,\nconditions will become life threatening as winds immediately return\nto dangerous speeds, so remain safely sheltered from the storm.\n\nDo not be a thrill seeker or risk your life for senseless photos or\nvideos.\n\nQuickly move to the safest place within your shelter if it begins to\nfail, preferably an interior room on the lowest floor as long as\nflooding is not a concern.\n\nIf you are prone to flooding or in an area under a storm surge watch\nor warning, be prepared for the possibility of a quick and dramatic\nrise in water levels.\n\nIf a tornado warning is issued for your area, quickly move to the\nsafest place within your shelter. Protect your head and body.\n\nIf an Extreme Wind Warning is issued for your area, move to the\nsafest place within your shelter. Take the same life-saving actions\nas if it were a violent tornado.\n\n* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:\n- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov\n- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org\n- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org\n\nNEXT UPDATE\n-----------\n\nThe next local statement will be issued by the National Weather\nService in Honolulu HI around 11 AM HST, or sooner if conditions\nwarrant.",

                "description": "* LOCATIONS AFFECTED\n- Hawaiian Ocean View Estates\n\n* WIND\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Equivalent Tropical Storm force wind\n- Peak Wind Forecast: 40-50 mph with gusts to 60 mph\n- Window for Tropical Storm force winds: until early Monday\nmorning\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 58\nto 73 mph\n- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the\nprevious assessment.\n- PLAN: Plan for dangerous wind of equivalent strong tropical\nstorm force.\n- PREPARE: Last minute efforts to protect life and property\nshould now be complete. The area remains subject to\nsignificant wind damage.\n- ACT: Now is the time to shelter from dangerous wind.\n\n- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Unfolding\n- Potential impacts from the main wind event are unfolding.\n\n* STORM SURGE\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Localized storm surge possible\n- Peak Storm Surge Inundation: The potential for 1-3 feet\nabove ground somewhere within surge prone areas\n- Window of concern: Begins early this morning\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for storm\nsurge flooding greater than 1 foot above ground\n- The storm surge threat has remained nearly steady from the\nprevious assessment.\n- PLAN: Plan for storm surge flooding greater than 1 foot\nabove ground.\n- PREPARE: Complete preparations for storm surge flooding,\nespecially in low-lying vulnerable areas, before conditions\nbecome unsafe.\n- ACT: Leave immediately if evacuation orders are given for\nyour area.\n\n- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Limited\n- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along\nimmediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas\nfarther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.\n- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become\noverspread with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous\nin places where surge water covers the road.\n- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes,\nmainly in usually vulnerable locations. A few small craft broken away from\nmoorings.\n\n* FLOODING RAIN\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Flood Watch is in effect\n- Peak Rainfall Amounts: Additional around 1 inch\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for\nmoderate flooding rain\n- The flooding rain threat has decreased from the previous\nassessment.\n- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for\nmoderate flooding from heavy rain. Evacuations and rescues\nare possible.\n- PREPARE: Consider protective actions if you are in an area\nvulnerable to flooding.\n- ACT: Heed any flood watches and warnings.                 "description": "* LOCATIONS AFFECTED\n- Hilo\n- Pahoa\n- Volcano\n\n* WIND\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Below tropical storm force wind\n- Peak Wind Forecast: 15-25 mph with gusts to 35 mph\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 58\nto 73 mph\n- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the\nprevious assessment.\n- PLAN: Plan for dangerous wind of equivalent strong tropical\nstorm force.\n- PREPARE: Remaining efforts to protect life and property\nshould be completed as soon as possible.                 "description": "* LOCATIONS AFFECTED\n- Bradshaw Army Airfield\n\n* WIND\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Below tropical storm force wind\n- Peak Wind Forecast: 25-35 mph with gusts to 50 mph\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 58\nto 73 mph\n- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the\nprevious assessment.\n- PLAN: Plan for dangerous wind of equivalent strong tropical\nstorm force.\n- PREPARE: Last minute efforts to protect life and property\nshould now be complete.                 "description": "* LOCATIONS AFFECTED\n- Kamuela\n- Hawi\n- Honokaa\n\n* WIND\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Equivalent Tropical Storm force wind\n- Peak Wind Forecast: 35-45 mph with gusts to 55 mph\n- Window for Tropical Storm force winds: until early Sunday\nmorning\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 58\nto 73 mph\n- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the\nprevious assessment.\n- PLAN: Plan for dangerous wind of equivalent strong tropical\nstorm force.\n- PREPARE: Last minute efforts to protect life and property\nshould now be complete. Driving conditions dangerous\nin places where surge water covers the road.\n- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes,\nmainly in usually vulnerable locations. Failure to take\naction may result in serious injury or loss of life.\n\n- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Significant\n- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations\nand rescues.\n- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with\nswifter currents and overspill their banks in a few places,\nespecially in usually vulnerable spots.                 "description": "* LOCATIONS AFFECTED\n- Naalehu\n- Pahala\n\n* WIND\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Equivalent Tropical Storm force wind\n- Peak Wind Forecast: 30-40 mph with gusts to 55 mph\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 58\nto 73 mph\n- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the\nprevious assessment.\n- PLAN: Plan for dangerous wind of equivalent strong tropical\nstorm force.\n- PREPARE: Last minute efforts to protect life and property\nshould now be complete. The area remains subject to\nsignificant wind damage.\n- ACT: Now is the time to shelter from dangerous wind.\n\n- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Unfolding\n- Potential impacts from the main wind event are unfolding.\n\n* STORM SURGE\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Localized storm surge possible\n- Peak Storm Surge Inundation: The potential for 1-3 feet\nabove ground somewhere within surge prone areas\n- Window of concern: Begins early this morning\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for storm\nsurge flooding greater than 1 foot above ground\n- The storm surge threat has remained nearly steady from the\nprevious assessment.\n- PLAN: Plan for storm surge flooding greater than 1 foot\nabove ground.\n- PREPARE: Complete preparations for storm surge flooding,\nespecially in low-lying vulnerable areas, before conditions\nbecome unsafe.\n- ACT: Leave immediately if evacuation orders are given for\nyour area.\n\n- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Limited\n- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along\nimmediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas\nfarther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.\n- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become\noverspread with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous\nin places where surge water covers the road.\n- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes,\nmainly in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.\n- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks,\nboardwalks, and piers. A few small craft broken away from\nmoorings.\n\n* FLOODING RAIN\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Flood Watch is in effect\n- Peak Rainfall Amounts: Additional 1-3 inches, with locally\nhigher amounts\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for\nmoderate flooding rain\n- The flooding rain threat has decreased from the previous\nassessment.\n- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for\nmoderate flooding from heavy rain. Evacuations and rescues\nare possible.\n- PREPARE: Consider protective actions if you are in an area\nvulnerable to flooding.\n- ACT: Heed any flood watches and warnings. Failure to take\naction may result in serious injury or loss of life.\n\n- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Significant\n- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations\nand rescues.\n- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with\nswifter currents and overspill their banks in a few places,\nespecially in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams,\ncreeks, canals, arroyos, and ditches overflow.\n- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken\nfoundations. Some streets and parking lots take on\nmoving water as storm drains and retention ponds overflow.\nDriving conditions become hazardous.                 "headline": "Hurricane Watch issued September 26 at 4:59AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI",
                "description": "* LOCATIONS AFFECTED\n- Hilo\n- Pahoa\n- Volcano\n\n* WIND\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Below tropical storm force wind\n- Peak Wind Forecast: 15-25 mph with gusts to 35 mph\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 58\nto 73 mph\n- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the\nprevious assessment.\n- PLAN: Plan for dangerous wind of equivalent strong tropical\nstorm force.\n- PREPARE: Remaining efforts to protect life and property\nshould be completed as soon as possible. Prepare for\nsignificant wind damage.\n- ACT: Move to safe shelter before the wind becomes hazardous.\n\n- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Significant\n- Some damage to roofing and siding materials, along with\ndamage to porches, awnings, carports, and sheds. A few\nbuildings experiencing window, door, and garage door\nfailures. Mobile homes damaged, especially if unanchored.\nUnsecured lightweight objects become dangerous projectiles.\n- Several large trees snapped or uprooted, but with greater\nnumbers in places where trees are shallow rooted. Several\nfences and roadway signs blown over.\n- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within\nurban or heavily wooded places. A few bridges, causeways,\nand access routes impassable.\n- Scattered power and communications outages, but more\nprevalent in areas with above ground lines.\n\n* STORM SURGE\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Localized storm surge possible\n- Peak Storm Surge Inundation: The potential for 1-3 feet\nabove ground somewhere within surge prone areas\n- Window of concern: Begins early this morning\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for storm\nsurge flooding greater than 1 foot above ground\n- The storm surge threat has remained nearly steady from the\nprevious assessment.\n- PLAN: Plan for storm surge flooding greater than 1 foot\nabove ground.\n- PREPARE: Complete preparations for storm surge flooding,\nespecially in low-lying vulnerable areas, before conditions\nbecome unsafe.\n- ACT: Leave immediately if evacuation orders are given for\nyour area.\n\n- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Limited\n- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along\nimmediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas\nfarther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.\n- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become\noverspread with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous\nin places where surge water covers the road.\n- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes,\nmainly in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.\n- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks,\nboardwalks, and piers. A few small craft broken away from\nmoorings.\n\n* FLOODING RAIN\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Flood Watch is in effect\n- Peak Rainfall Amounts: Additional 2-4 inches, with locally\nhigher amounts\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for\nmoderate flooding rain\n- The flooding rain threat has decreased from the previous\nassessment.\n- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for\nmoderate flooding from heavy rain. Evacuations and rescues\nare possible.\n- PREPARE: Consider protective actions if you are in an area\nvulnerable to flooding.\n- ACT: Heed any flood watches and warnings. Failure to take\naction may result in serious injury or loss of life.\n\n- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Significant\n- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations\nand rescues.\n- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with\nswifter currents and overspill their banks in a few places,\nespecially in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams,\ncreeks, canals, arroyos, and ditches overflow.\n- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken\nfoundations. Several places may experience expanded areas\nof rapid inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and\npoor drainage areas. Some streets and parking lots take on\nmoving water as storm drains and retention ponds overflow.\nDriving conditions become hazardous. Some road and bridge\nclosures.\n\n* TORNADO\n- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST:\n- Situation is somewhat favorable for tornadoes\n\n- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST\nUNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for a few\ntornadoes\n- The tornado threat has remained nearly steady from the\nprevious assessment.\n- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for a\nfew tornadoes.\n- PREPARE: If your shelter is particularly vulnerable to\ntornadoes, prepare to relocate to safe shelter before\nhazardous weather arrives.\n- ACT: If a tornado warning is issued, be ready to shelter\nquickly.\n\n- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Limited\n- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the\nexecution of emergency plans during tropical events.\n- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with\npower and communications disruptions.\n- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings,\nchimneys toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or\noverturned, large tree tops and branches snapped off,\nshallow-rooted trees knocked over, moving vehicles blown\noff roads, and small boats pulled from moorings.\n\n* FOR MORE INFORMATION:\n- https://www.weather.gov/hfo",

                "description": "Hurricane Nolo remains nearly stationary south of the Big Island.\nThe possibility of heavy rain could lead to localized flooding over\nportions of the Big Island and Maui.\n\n* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.\n\n* WHERE...Big Island, Maui, Lanai, Molokai, and Kahoolawe.\n\n* WHEN...Through this afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Flood prone roads and other low lying areas may be closed\ndue to elevated runoff and overflowing streams. Urban areas may\nreceive more significant flooding and property damage due to rapid\nrunoff. Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of\nstreams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along\nwith property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.\nLandslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- The possibility remains for localized flooding over areas of the\nBig Island and Maui due to heavy rain from slow moving Hurricane\nNolo to the south of the Big Island.                 "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
                "senderName": "NWS Melbourne FL",
                "headline": "Flood Warning issued September 26 at 9:37AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL",
                "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\n\nSt Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.\n\n.The St Johns River at Astor remains within Minor Flood Stage and is\nforecast to continue to rise, cresting on Sunday due to an ongoing\nperiod of northerly winds and tidal effects. River levels are\nforecast to then gradually subside through Minor Flood Stage through\nthe middle of next week.\n\nFor the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon\nFish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water\napproaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and\nAstor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river\nwater south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor\nBridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are\ncovered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud\nroads are underwater with yards inundated.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 2.7 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 8:30 AM EDT Saturday was 2.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 2.8 feet\nthis weekend.\n- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.9\nfeet on 10/17/1999.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nCaution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.",

                "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
                "senderName": "NWS Honolulu HI",
                "headline": "Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 25 at 11:15PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI",
                "description": "HLSHFO\n\nThis product covers the Hawaiian islands\n\n**HURRICANE NOLO REMAINS STATIONARY SOUTH OF THE BIG ISLAND**\n\nNEW INFORMATION\n---------------\n\n* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:\n- None\n\n* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:\n- A Tropical Storm Warning and Hurricane Watch are in effect for\nBig Island East, Big Island Interior, Big Island North, Big\nIsland South, Big Island Southeast, Big Island Summits, Kohala,\nand Kona\n- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Haleakala Summit,\nKahoolawe, Kipahulu, Lanai Leeward, Lanai Mauka, Lanai South,\nLanai Windward, Maui Central Valley North, Maui Central Valley\nSouth, Maui Leeward West, Maui Windward West, Molokai Leeward\nSouth, Molokai North, Molokai Southeast, Molokai West, Molokai\nWindward, South Haleakala, South Maui/Upcountry, and Windward\nHaleakala\n\n* STORM INFORMATION:\n- About 350 miles south-southeast of Honolulu or about 200 miles\nsouth of Hilo\n- 16.9N 155.3W\n- Storm Intensity 105 mph\n- Movement Stationary\n\nSITUATION OVERVIEW\n------------------\n\nNearly stationary, Hurricane Nolo is expected to strengthen into a\nmajor hurricane as it turns westward and accelerates Saturday and\nSunday. Nolo is forecast to track northward early next week and could\ncontinue to intensify. While the center will stay well south and west\nof the state, impacts will extend far outside the center of Nolo.\n\nBands of intense showers and thunderstorms will bring 8 to 12 inches\nwith localized higher amounts of 16 inches of rainfall to windward and\nsoutheast portions of the Big Island. This heavy rainfall will cause\nsignificant, life-threatening flash flooding and mudslides,\nparticularly in areas of steep terrain. Heavy rain will spread to Maui\nby Saturday, brining 4 to 6 inches with localized amounts up to\n8 inches possible, especially over steep terrain. Terrain-enhanced\nrainfall from outer rain bands may also reach the rest of the state.\n\nTropical storm force winds and gusts are occurring on the Big Island,\nwith hurricane force winds possible by early Saturday, especially over\ncomplex terrain. A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Maui County,\nwhere tropical storm force winds and gusts are occurring. Strong,\ngusty winds will affect all Hawaiian Islands through the weekend, and a\nWind Advisory takes effect for the rest of the state starting Saturday\nmorning.\n\nSwells generated by Nolo will bring dangerously large, rough surf and\nsevere rip currents, especially for southeast and east facing shores\nof the Big Island. A High Surf Advisory remains in effect for south\nand east facing shores of Big Island and east facing shores of Maui\nand Molokai, as well as east-facing shores of Kauai and Oahu.\n\nTornadoes and waterspouts are possible near and over the Big Island,\nprimarily to the right of the track of Nolo.\n\nPOTENTIAL IMPACTS\n-----------------\n\n* FLOODING RAIN:\nProtect against life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible\nextensive impacts across windward and southeast Big Island. Potential\nimpacts include:\n- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.\n- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in\nmultiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, arroyos, and\nditches may become dangerous rivers. In mountain areas,\ndestructive runoff may run quickly down valleys while\nincreasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides. Flood\ncontrol systems and barriers may become stressed.\n- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple\ncommunities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed\naway. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.\nStreets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with\nunderpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.\nMany road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.\n\nProtect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible limited\nto significant impacts across leeward Big Island and Maui Island.\n\nElsewhere across the Hawaiian islands, little to no impact is\nanticipated.\n\n* WIND:\nProtect against dangerous wind having possible significant impacts\nacross Big Island. Potential impacts in this area include:\n- Some damage to roofing and siding materials, along with damage\nto porches, awnings, carports, and sheds. A few buildings\nexperiencing window, door, and garage door failures. Mobile\nhomes damaged, especially if unanchored. Unsecured lightweight\nobjects become dangerous projectiles.\n- Several large trees snapped or uprooted, but with greater\nnumbers in places where trees are shallow rooted. Several\nfences and roadway signs blown over.\n- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban\nor heavily wooded places. A few bridges, causeways, and access\nroutes impassable.\n- Scattered power and communications outages, but more prevalent\nin areas with above ground lines.\n\nAlso, protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts\nacross the rest of the main Hawaiian Islands.\n\n* SURGE:\nProtect against locally hazardous surge having possible limited impacts\nacross Big Island. Potential impacts in this area include:\n- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along\nimmediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas\nfarther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.\n- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread\nwith surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where\nsurge water covers the road.\n- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly\nin usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.\n- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,\nand piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.\n\nElsewhere across the Hawaiian islands, little to no impact is\nanticipated.\n\n* TORNADOES:\nProtect against a tornado event having possible limited impacts across\nBig Island. Potential impacts include:\n- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution\nof emergency plans during tropical events.\n- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power\nand communications disruptions.\n- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys\ntoppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,\nlarge tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees\nknocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats\npulled from moorings.\n\nPRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS\n----------------------------------\n\n* EVACUATIONS:\nFollow the advice of local officials\n\n* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:\nNow is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and\nproperty in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a\nsafe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.\n\nIf you are relocating to safe shelter, leave as early as possible.\nAllow extra time to reach your destination. Many roads and bridges\nwill be closed once strong winds arrive. Check the latest weather\nforecast before departing and drive with caution.\n\nIf heading to a community shelter, become familiar with the shelter\nrules before arrival, especially if you have special needs or have\npets. Take essential items with you from your Emergency Supplies Kit.\n\nFailure to adequately shelter may result in serious injury or loss of\nlife. Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with any\norders that are issued. Be patient and helpful with those you encounter.\n\nIf you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in\nwhich you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which\nit resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay\nattention for instructions from local authorities.\n\nStorm surge is the leading killer associated with tropical storms and\nhurricanes! Remember, turn around don't drown!\n\nIf a Tornado Warning is issued for your area, be ready to shelter\nquickly, preferably away from windows and in an interior room not\nprone to flooding.                 "description": "* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, one to two feet and\nlocally up to 2 1/2 feet of inundation above ground level in\nvulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.                 "headline": "Hydrologic Outlook issued September 25 at 2:21PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO",
                "description": "ESFGJT\n\nIn the wake of today's precipitation, our attention will turn to the\nEastern Pacific. Tropical moisture is anticipated to spread across\nthe Desert Southwest early next week, drawing moisture from a pair of\nHurricanes; Odalys and Polo. The forecast becomes increasing complex\ndue to a closed low currently forecast to drive across the Southwest\nCONUS as Hurricane Polo approaches the Baja California Peninsula.\nStrong southerly winds ahead of the low are expected to pull tropical\nmoisture towards eastern Utah and western Colorado as early as Monday\nmorning. The challenge and uncertainty in our precipitation forecast\nincrease as the week progresses and the low traverses our southern\nStates. Excessive rainfall is most probable over AZ and NM, attm, but\nthe northerly extent poses a threat to our southern San Juan river\nbasins. Current forecasts suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain over Monday\nmorning through Wednesday. At face value, rivers and tributaries will\nsee a bump up due to said moisture. However, localized heavier\namounts could result in minor flooding across the southern San Juan\nfoothills and communities further downstream.\n\nRivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated\nsoils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of\nadditional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar\nresponse. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in\nseveral creeks and rivers than what has been observed over the\nprevious 7 days. However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts\n(i.e. above 90th percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action\nstage to minor flooding. Most probable basins to see significant\nrises include; the Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito\nCreek, and the Animas River Basins.\n\nConvective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said\ntropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across\nthe CWA, however, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San\nJuans. Please continue to monitor the forecast as these systems\nevolve. Especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in\nthe southwest quadrant of the forecast area.",
